item.title: Using a Self-Hosted Git Repository as a Maven Repository
item.author: me@codeskraps.com (codeskraps)
item.description: If you maintain shared libraries across multiple Android or Kotlin Multiplatform projects, you’ve probably considered publishing them to a Maven repository. Maven Central works, but the publishing process is heavy — GPG signing, Sonatype staging, approval delays. For private or small-scale libraries, that’s overkill. If you already self-host a Git server like Gitea or Gogs, you can use it as a Maven repository with zero additional infrastructure.

item.title: Umami Analytics for Mobile Apps Without a WebView
item.author: me@codeskraps.com (codeskraps)
item.description: Umami is a great privacy-focused, self-hosted alternative to Google Analytics. But its documentation assumes you’re tracking a website. If you want to use it in a mobile app, the docs point you toward embedding a WebView — which is clunky, adds overhead, and feels wrong for native apps. There’s a better way: hit the Umami API directly.

item.title: React Native vs Kotlin Multiplatform
item.author: me@codeskraps.com (codeskraps)
item.description:
Introduction

In the ever-evolving world of mobile app development, choosing the right cross-platform framework can be a game-changer for businesses and developers alike. Two prominent contenders in this space are React Native and Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP). Both offer unique approaches to the challenge of writing code once and deploying it across multiple platforms. This article will dive deep into the strengths and considerations of each, helping you make an informed decision for your next project.

item.title: Configuring SSH Keys for Individual Git Commands
item.author: me@codeskraps.com (codeskraps)
item.description: When working with Git repositories, you often need to authenticate using SSH keys. item.title: Projects
item.author: me@codeskraps.com (codeskraps)
item.description:
FreqDroid

A mobile client for FreqTrade, the open-source cryptocurrency trading bot framework. Monitor and manage all your trading bots from your phone.

Features

  • Multi-Bot Dashboard: Aggregate open trades, profit charts, and performance across all your bots on a single screen
  • Detailed Analytics: Trade logs, pair breakdowns, balance history, cumulative profit, and candlestick charts with technical indicators
  • Flexible Navigation: Choose between Aggregate (flat all-in-one) or Classic (sectioned dashboard) interface modes
  • Push Notifications: Instant trade alerts via ntfy — self-hosted, your server, your data
  • Customization: HSL color picker, Material You dynamic theming, light/dark/system themes

Built with Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform. Available on Google Play — iOS coming soon. Visit freqdroid.com for more details.
